claim_being_audited: That the current release can be certified on a qualified basis if the unresolved mental health referral routing weakness is explicitly disclosed in the model card, rather than treating the release as having no material limitations.
decision_criteria: Verdict would improve if admissible evidence directly showed that qualified certification with explicit disclosure is allowed under internal policy.
Verdict would improve if the cited evidence substantiated the claimed aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one incidents, and bounded nature of the unresolved weakness.
Verdict would improve if there were an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Verdict would worsen if the underlying evidence showed the weakness is material to named launch use cases without an approval path for launch.
Verdict would worsen if the cited public guidance was used to substitute for missing internal authorization or missing operational controls.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of each cited evidence item, especially the policy text, aggregate readiness results, current-gap evidence, and near-miss details.
Provide the exact model-card draft or release artifact showing the proposed limitation disclosure language.
Provide any internal policy provision or approval path that expressly permits certification with a disclosed unresolved material limitation.
Provide evidence of whether a formal risk acceptance exists or was denied for this issue.
Provide concrete impact evidence for the mental health referral routing weakness: severity, frequency, affected use cases, and whether rollback criteria were considered.
specific_concerns: The audit is based only on the Actor's summary, not the underlying admissible evidence, so key predicates cannot be independently verified.

The policy text provided clearly sets conditions for certification without material caveats, but does not itself establish that qualified certification is permitted under the current unresolved weakness.

The mitigation artifact is described as a draft with owner and threshold still TBD, which is expressly insufficient to remove a current disclosure requirement and may also indicate incomplete operational control.

The Actor's packet appears to rely on external governance guidance to support disclosure and monitoring, but that guidance does not by itself prove internal policy authorization for certification now.

The materiality and scope of the mental health referral routing weakness are asserted in summary form, but the underlying severity, affected traffic, and launch-use-case impact are not independently shown.
unsupported_claims: That aggregate readiness clearing by 2.1 percentage points and no severity-one rehearsal incidents are sufficient support for certification of this release.
That the remaining weakness is sufficiently bounded to permit certification rather than requiring resolution or formal risk acceptance.
That public model-card and AI risk-management guidance materially support the internal certification decision beyond supporting disclosure and monitoring practice.
That certification is affirmatively allowed under the stated policy on the present record, as opposed to only making a weaker disclosure-required case against a no-limitations representation.
